name: Lan Na Kingdom
native: เมืองล้านนา (Mueang Lanna)
alt: Kingdom of a Million Rice Fields

predecessors.name: Ngoenyang
predecessors.text: Mangrai's Ngoenyang around Chiang Rai (founded 1262 as his capital), which became Lan Na

predecessors.name: Haripuñjaya
predecessors.text: the Mon kingdom of Hariphunchai (Lamphun), annexed in 1292 (Lan Na infobox)

successors.name: Lan Na
successors.text: the same state and the same land (180 cells) after Mekuti's capture in November 1564: Lan Na under Burmese suzerainty, to the Siamese conquest of 15 January 1775 (Lan Na infobox)

ledger.x: 1292: Mangrai's Ngoenyang becomes the kingdom of Lan Na with the annexation of Haripunjaya.
1338: Khamfu of Chiang Saen annexes Phayao.
1353: Fa Ngum beats Lan Na at Chiang Saen.
1451: Sawankhalok breaks away from Ayutthaya and joins Lan Na; Lan Na besieges Chaliang.
1452: Ayutthaya withdraws from Chiang Mai after Lan Xang helps Lan Na.
1474: Lan Na retakes Chienjuen, 'putting an end to the conflict'.
1546: a prince of Lan Xang takes the throne of Lan Na.
1551: Mekuti becomes king of Lan Na.
November 1564: Mekuti is captured; the dossier stops (a boundary of the data, not the end of the state).

wars.name: Mangrai's conquest of Haripunjaya
wars.outcome: Haripunjaya annexed to Lan Na; Yi Ba, the last king, fled south to Lampang.

wars.name: Khamfu's annexation of Phayao
wars.outcome: Phayao annexed into Lan Na, its eastern cities into Nan.

wars.name: Fa Ngum's war against Lan Na
wars.outcome: Fa Ngum overwhelmed Phayu's army at Chiang Saen and Lan Na ceded some territory.

wars.name: Ayutthaya-Lan Na War (1441-1474)
wars.outcome: Stalemate with limited territorial gains for Lan Na; Ayutthaya captured Chiang Mai in 1452 and withdrew; Lan Na took Sawankhalok in 1459; Ayutthaya reconquered Phrae in 1460; Lan Na retook Chienjuen in 1474.

wars.name: Ayutthayan invasions of Lan Na (1507, 1513)
wars.outcome: Kaew's invasion of Ayutthaya (1507) was repelled; Ramathibodi II invaded Lan Na in 1513 and sacked Lampang; no border change.

wars.name: Toungoo subjugation of Lan Na
wars.outcome: Mekuti surrendered on 2 April 1558 and Lan Na 'became a vassal state of the Toungoo dynasty in 1558'; he stayed king until 'captured by Burmese forces in November 1564'.

certainty.note: A mandala of mueang around the Ping and Kok valleys: no treaty or survey fixes the frontier.
